neighbours.label: a fixed list of rare word-completions, not rare-word endings in general: Kn|op|f, atr|azine, Arbit|ron, acros|ome fire; look-alike endings (ribosome, lysosome, simazine, Nielsen, Scribner) stay quiet
fire: Her first novel was bought by Knopf after a short auction.
Traces of atrazine were found in wells near the cornfields.
For decades Arbitron ratings decided which radio hosts kept their jobs.
Enzymes released from the acrosome let the sperm pass through the egg's coat.
The memoir came out from Alfred A. Knopf in the autumn of 2003.
European regulators banned atrazine because it lingers in groundwater.
Stations paid Arbitron to survey listeners in each local market.
In the mature sperm the acrosome sits like a cap over the nucleus.
quiet: Her first novel was bought by Scribner after a short auction.
Traces of simazine were found in wells near the cornfields.
For decades Nielsen ratings decided which television hosts kept their jobs.
Enzymes stored in the lysosome let the cell digest worn-out parts.
The memoir came out from Penguin in the autumn of 2003.
European regulators banned glyphosate on roadside verges last year.
Stations paid Gallup to survey listeners in each local market.
In the mature neuron the ribosome sits along the rough membrane.

notes: Card: no single token ('kle','b','LOY','op','m','ome'), every top example the completing piece of an uncommon name or term. Probes: Knopf 1.00, Arbitron 1.03, atrazine 0.90, Kolm 0.88, acrosome 0.71, Aksay 0.70; ten new rare completions (glyphosate, ribosome, lysosome, centrosome, Nabokov, Scribner, Lindqvist, simazine, Nielsen, Kellogg) all < 0.06. So the shared pattern 'last piece of a rare word' does NOT hold on new cases; only the list holds, and the list here is certainly incomplete (the card's 32 top examples have many more items). Early layer: word-identity completion.
